definitions.explanation: A mistake or transgression, often with moral or serious implications. Carries a heavier, more literary tone than simply 間違い and implies personal responsibility.

examples.japanese: {同|おな}じ{過|あやま}ちを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}すな。
{若|わか}い{頃|ころ}の{過|あやま}ちを{悔|く}やんでいる。
examples.english: I regret the mistakes I made when I was young.

examples.japanese: {戦争|せんそう}という{過|あやま}ちを{二度|にど}と{繰|く}り{返|かえ}してはならないと、{多|おお}くの{人|ひと}が{訴|うった}えている。
examples.english: Many people are calling for the mistake of war to never be repeated.

notes:
USAGE NOTES:
{過|あやま}ち has a more serious and literary tone than {間違|まちが}い (mistake). It implies moral weight — a failing, a transgression, or a grave error — rather than a simple factual mistake.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {過|あやま}ちを{犯|おか}す (to commit a mistake/transgression)
- {過|あやま}ちを{繰|く}り{返|かえ}す (to repeat a mistake)
- {過|あやま}ちを{認|みと}める (to acknowledge one's fault)
- {若|わか}い{頃|ころ}の{過|あやま}ち (mistakes of youth)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{間違|まちが}い is neutral and covers any kind of mistake. {過|あやま}ち implies moral responsibility and is often used in reflective, regretful, or admonitory contexts.
